faq.q: What jewelry photo should I upload?
faq.a: Use a sharp photo of the complete piece on a plain surface. Keep the chain, clasp, stones, and mount visible.

faq.q: Can I show how a necklace sits?
faq.a: Yes. Choose a scene at the neck and keep the chain in the photo. Put the measured length and the material in the listing text.

faq.q: Which pieces work in a worn photo?
faq.a: Necklaces, earrings on a person, rings, bracelets, and cufflinks work when your photo shows their shape and surface. If a detail is cut off in your photo, the new photo can get it wrong.

faq.q: How do I keep a stone or clasp accurate?
faq.a: Compare the download with your original at full size. Keep a version whose stone, mount, clasp, and color still match. Do not keep a photo that adds a prong or changes the metal. A prong is the little claw on a stone.

faq.q: Can I remove the background and add light?
faq.a: Yes. Clear the table and the props, then add a shadow and a light that leave gold and stones readable. Check the edge before you publish.

faq.q: Can one setup cover many pieces?
faq.a: Yes. Run the same background, shadow, and framing on many photos at once, or start them from your own software (the API). Each photo is 24 credits, shown before you start.

faq.q: Do I need to hire a jewelry model?
faq.a: No. The worn scene is generated from your piece photo. The person or the hand is AI, not a booked model and not a customer.

faq.q: What does a jewelry photo cost?
faq.a: Each photo costs 24 credits. Starter is $24.50 a month with 200 credits. You see the cost before you start. If it fails, those credits come back. The download has no watermark, and you can use it in your ads, pages, and posts.

faq.q: Can I try the API on one piece first?
faq.a: Yes. Upload one jewelry photo and try a background removal, a shadow, or a worn photo. Read the 24-credit cost before you send a larger catalog.

faq.q: What if I also need a scene with no person?
faq.a: Use a table scene when size on a body is not the point. Photos with no person are on the [AI lifestyle product photos](page:lifestyle-photos) page.
